message.content:
To terminate Visual Studio Code (the `code.exe` process) from the command line you can use the built‑in Windows utility **taskkill**.

```cmd
:: Kill all instances of VS Code forcefully
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

### What each part means

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `/IM`    | Specifies the image name (process executable). In this case `code.exe`. |
| `/F`     | Forces termination (equivalent to “End Process” in Task Manager). |

If you only want to kill a specific instance, first find its PID:

```cmd
:: List all running processes and filter for code.exe
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This will show something like:

```
Image Name                     PID Session Name        Session#    Mem Usage
========================= ======== ================ ========= ============
code.exe                    12345 Console                 1      150,000 K
```

Then kill that particular PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID 12345 /F
```

### Common pitfalls

* **Permissions** – If you’re not running the command prompt as an administrator, you may get “Access denied”. Right‑click “Command Prompt” → “Run as administrator”.
* **Multiple instances** – `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` kills *all* `code.exe` processes. If you have multiple VS Code windows open and only want to close one, use the PID method above.
* **Background services** – Some extensions or background tasks may spawn additional processes (`node.exe`, `python.exe`, etc.). Those won’t be killed by targeting `code.exe` alone.

That’s it! Use the command(s) above to stop VS Code from the command line.
